labels.note: The highlighted text (item c under 9-2. Cooking) does state 'the starting water weight shall be at least 96.00 oz (2.721 kg)', so the value, unit and minimum wording are faithful. However, the claim attributes this requirement to Contest 9-3 Dinner Party, when it is a rule of the 9-2 Cooking subcontest; the same sentence's 'single container' requirement and the kg equivalent were also not captured.

The source shows Table 5-1, titled 'Drivetrain Properties,' which lists rated rotor and generator speeds, gearbox ratio, generator efficiency and inertia, driveshaft torsional spring and damping constants, and high-speed shaft brake torque and time constant. The statement accurately summarizes this scope and role without quoting any values or design decisions, and the keywords cover every row of the table.

The FFA-W3-211 77% span chart shows the pressure side as a multi-material layup (medium_density_foam core with glass_triax and glass_uni layers near the TE), so glass_triax is only one of several materials there, not the composition of the pressure side. The quoted text is merely a legend label and does not state this binding, and no s-coordinate range is given for where glass_triax actually occurs.

A defines the vertical datum (GRADE LEVEL = 0") on sheet S-522 of one document (dc-cd), while B gives the Bedroom finished floor height (2'-9 1/2") relative to GRADE LEVEL on sheet A-303 of a different document (calg-cd). Because the two sources are different projects/proposals, the grade-level datum A establishes is not demonstrably the datum B is measured from, so the claims cannot be treated as compatible information about one corresponding elevation system.

Figure 9 plots 'Points per cooking task' against 'Weight of vaporized water (oz)'; the curve is flat from 0 to 20 oz, rises linearly from 20 to 80 oz, then flattens, so 20 oz is indeed where the linear increase begins. However, 20 is an x-axis weight (oz), not a 'points per cooking task' value, so the attribute label is wrong, and the quoted text is only the axis label and does not state the value 20. The figure also belongs to 9-2. Cooking (Figure 9, Cooking Subcontest), not 9-3. Dinner Party as the context claims, and the nearby legend thresholds (no points ≤ 16 oz, full points ≥ 80 oz) were not extracted.

Claim A is from the NREL 5-MW document (Table 7-1, pitch angle 23.47° at 25.0 m/s), while Claim B is from the IEA 15-MW document (blade pitch controller objective of 7.55 rpm rated speed over 10.59–25 m/s). Both quotes are accurate as shown, but they describe the blade pitch controllers of two different turbines and different properties (pitch angle value vs. control objective), so they are not compatible information about a corresponding subject and the retrieval pairing is not sensible.

Table 4-1 (Material Properties for the Tower) lists 'Young's modulus, steel' with symbol E and value '2 00E11 Pa', i.e. 2.00E11 Pa, exactly as claimed. The quote is a faithful rendering of the table row (parameter, symbol, value, units stitched together), and the value, unit and entity all match the source.

The figure shows the blade cross section at 70% span (Section: 0.7) with a legend of six materials — Medium Density Foam, Glass Triax, Glass Biax, Carbon UD, Glass Uni and Gelcoat — used in different regions of the section. Carbon UD is only one of several materials in the layup, so recording the section's material composition as simply 'Carbon UD' overstates a single legend entry as the whole composition, and the quote 'Carbon UD' (a legend label) does not support that composition claim.

The source's STRUCTURAL ENGINEER block lists Bob Allison, PE, Arup Engineering at 1120 Connecticut Avenue, NW., Suite 200, Washington, DC 20036, so the address value and its binding to the Structural Engineer are correct. The quote is simply the line-wrapped address reflowed onto one line, with no content altered, so it remains faithful.

The highlighted sentence states the resulting gains for the baseline blade-pitch controller as K_P(θ = 0°) = 0.01882681 s, K_I(θ = 0°) = 0.008068634, and K_D = 0.0 s², so the quoted value, entity and θ = 0° condition are read faithfully and verbatim. The same sentence also gives K_P(θ = 0°) = 0.01882681 s and K_D = 0.0 s² (and the ζ_φ = 0.7 damping-ratio choice), which are not covered by this item.

Figure 10 and the accompanying table confirm that full points (100, the top of the y-axis 'Points at conclusion of Energy Balance Contest') are awarded at a net electrical energy of 0 kWh (indeed for ≥ 0 kWh), so the core value is right. However, the 'quote' is stitched together from the two axis labels plus tick values (100, 0) and is not verbatim text from the source, and the value is marked approximate although the table states full points exactly. Nearby, the reduced-points band (-50 to 0 kWh, linear) and the no-points threshold (≤ -50 kWh) were not extracted.

The figure is Figure 10, the scoring function for the Energy Balance Contest, plotting points at conclusion of the contest against net electrical energy (kWh), with full points, a linearly reduced region, and a no-points region. The 'about' statement is accurate and useful, but the role statement names specific values and the linear-scaling design decision, and it covers only the reduced-points region rather than the whole scoring function.

The highlighted table (Figure 9 scoring function for the Cooking Subcontest) does state 'No points: Weight ≤ 16 oz (450 g)' for the weight of vaporized water, so the value, unit and inequality direction are read correctly. However, this table belongs to section 9-2 Cooking, not 9-3 Dinner Party as the claim's condition and section context assert, and the sibling rows (full points ≥ 80 oz, reduced points 16–80 oz) were not extracted.

Detail E6 (ROOF BEAM @ GRID 2,3,4) shows a vertical dimension stack of 2", 6", 2" at the opening, so the opening sits 2" below the top edge of the beam. The claim's entity, value (2"), unit and detail reference all match the drawing, and the topmost 2" dimension is the offset from the top edge.

The source shows the level marker 'FINISHED FLOOR 2' - 3"' (2 ft 3 in) on the exterior elevations, including the West Elevation, but the claim records the elevation as 2 ft. Dropping the 3-inch component makes the value wrong (2 ft vs 2'-3" = 2.25 ft), even though the quote itself is verbatim and the entity/attribute binding is fine.

Sheet A-301 is titled BUILDING SECTIONS and shows two section drawings labeled 'SECTION - WEST MODULE' and 'SECTION - EAST MODULE', each annotated with finished floor and grade level elevation markers. The statement correctly identifies the drawing type, the two modules covered, and the level datums shown, without quoting any elevation values or design decisions.

The highlighted region covers the empty 'REFERENCE KEYNOTES' and 'SHEET KEYNOTES' boxes on sheet S-701, which contain no text at all — no 'C1 3/16"' row or table is visible there. The quoted string and the thickness value are not present in the shown source, so the claim is unsupported (a 'C1' detail bubble exists on the drawing, but no thickness is attached to it).
